title: A dataset's table
description: The shape of the table an object owns (docs/unoverse/data/objects/dataset.md). The declaration IS the schema: it generates a migration a person reviews, and nobody edits a database schema by hand.

description.description: What one row of this table is.

columns.description: The columns, in the order they are written. A name the platform puts on every dataset itself (id, org, of, document, created_at, updated_at) may not be declared here.

name.description: Lower case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter: a plain word that never has to be quoted.

type.description: `number` is exact decimal and never floating point, so a total that must reconcile against a stated figure does not drift.

required.description: A row without it is refused at the door.

indexed.description: Searched, filtered or grouped by, so the generated table indexes it.

description.description: What this column holds, in the words a reader of the data would use.

enum.description: The only values this column may hold. The database refuses anything else, so a word that IS the language (a measure, a unit, a side) cannot arrive misspelled and quietly become a second thing that never adds up with the first. Leave it off for a column that carries a document's own words, which are not ours to enumerate.

uniqueBy.description: The columns that together identify one row, so a read again replaces its rows rather than landing beside them and counting a reading twice.

subject.description: The column that says WHOSE these rows are. The one row this dataset leaves on the map is titled from it; the platform never guesses the word.

asOf.description: The column that says when these rows speak as of, so the handle can say it.
